priority_policy.name: buyer_question_relevance
priority_policy.rule: Claims whose canonical category is directly relevant to the buyer's stated goal (e.g. nearby_amenities/address for nearby_services_check).
priority_policy.applies_only_when: buyer_goal narrows relevance (family_suitability, price_validation, nearby_services_check); general_question/fast_claim_triage do not narrow.

priority_policy.name: tool_checkable
priority_policy.rule: Canonical category is in TOOLS_BY_VERIFIABLE_CATEGORY (nearby_amenities, price_comparison).

priority_policy.name: transaction_structure_and_future_commitments
priority_policy.rule: Canonical category == transaction_structure (rent-then-purchase, purchase option, future price terms).

priority_policy.name: seller_or_document_verification
priority_policy.rule: condition claims, or factual claims with no canonical category (e.g. floor).

priority_policy.name: redundant_with_property_details
priority_policy.rule: address/price/rooms/size_sqm claims (only the first survives dedup; a second is removed entirely before ranking).

deduplication_policy.exact_text_duplicate: normalized (trimmed, case-folded, whitespace-collapsed) text duplicates are removed regardless of category.
deduplication_policy.redundant_with_property_details: a second+ claim in address/price/rooms/size_sqm categories is removed - the first representative claim is kept, the structured PropertyDetails field already carries the value for every downstream consumer.
deduplication_policy.never_merged_by_broad_category: condition claims (safe room, parquet, kitchen, bathroom, ...) are never merged with each other just because they share the 'condition' category - each is an independent commitment.

missing_information_examples: whether rent is credited toward the purchase price
whether the purchase is optional or binding

stability: Ties within the same priority bucket preserve post-dedup order (Python's stable sort) - never re-derived from raw LLM list position alone.
